title: Define infrastructure boundary and provider-neutral port contracts V1
businessObjective: Keep guest operations isolated while Staff and AI OS infrastructure can change through adapters and configuration without a domain rewrite.
technicalObjective: Implement one closed static V1 structural authority, one canonical trust-zone policy artifact, and one runtime-safe validation deep module for finite cross-zone descriptors and provider-neutral ports; do not provision, integrate, authenticate, dispatch, or select infrastructure.
assumptions: P2-005 remains static Tier-0 contract validation only; a successful descriptor validation is not authentication, authorization, approval, capacity reservation, dispatch permission, or evidence of a live recipient check.

The public module obtains the committed schema and canonical policy internally and accepts no caller-supplied authority, validator, adapter, configuration, credential verifier, clock, state store, rate limiter, quota state, or dependency injection.
No account, domain, service, provider, credential, network, database, queue, deployment, production integration, or external system is selected, accessed, or configured.
P2-006 and P2-007 will separately define minimisation/retention and numeric budget authorities; P2-005 must not invent them.
acceptanceCriteria: `schemas/infrastructure-port-contract-v1.schema.json` is one closed Draft 2020-12 authority for the exact canonical policy and boundary-request structures in the GOV-047 design; every object is closed and all finite values and bounds are explicit.

`policies/infrastructure-trust-zone-policy-v1.json` validates under the schema and fixes exactly the guest/public, staff/control, and AI/workload zones; distinct credential/quota/deployment/failure boundaries; authenticated HTTPS protocol bounds; five directed route classes; booking isolation; dependency rules; and non-authority posture.

The canonical policy declares exactly thirteen provider-neutral ports and their finite V1 operations: persistence, ingestion, analytics, scheduling/queues, workflow, object storage, notifications, intelligence, deployment, authentication, proposal generation, executor adapters, and verification; core imports no infrastructure/provider SDK or configuration and providers gain no policy, authorization, workflow, approval, or audit authority.

`packages/infrastructure-contracts/src/infrastructure-port-contract-v1.mjs` exports only `validateInfrastructureBoundaryRequest(request)`, obtains committed authority internally, returns deeply frozen plain-data decisions, mutates no input, ignores caller dependency arguments, and never throws for any JavaScript input.

Validation deterministically fails closed for malformed input, unsupported version/zone/route/port, zone or route confusion, insecure or unbounded transport, missing/invalid/expired/mis-audienced credentials, invalid timestamp, missing/reused nonce, missing/conflicting/duplicate idempotency, caller/route saturation or unknown metering, shared boundaries, booking-capacity dependency, provider/self authority claims, and caller authority injection using the exact reason precedence in the design.

The module and documentation state that network-supplied facts are untrusted; live recipient adapters must independently establish cryptographic identity, time, replay/idempotency history, rate/quota state, and isolation before later policy/approval dispatch. Validation success alone never dispatches.

The implementation creates only the exact schema, policy, deep module, validator, product documentation, P2-005 evidence/state, and permitted risk update; it adds no adapter, SDK, endpoint, service, provider, storage, workflow, credential, rate limiter, deployment, migration, production behavior, or external call.

The exact admitted validator compiles the committed schema, validates the canonical policy, tests every finite value/bound/mapping and focused exploit path, proves private authority, total/frozen/clone behavior and import boundaries, and passes with packet validation, fast verification, diff checks, independent Sol QA, task-specific machine evidence, and final-head CI.
allowedCommands: npm run verify:task -- --task SUT-AIOS-P2-005 --verifier-agent qa-verification --verifier-model gpt-5.6-sol --acceptance-confirmed
requiredChecks: closed Draft 2020-12 schema compilation and canonical policy validation
finite trust-zone, route, protocol, port, operation, isolation, and authority review
deep-module private-authority and hexagonal import-boundary inspection
focused authentication, replay, idempotency, limit, booking-isolation, and caller-authority exploit regressions
malformed and hostile input never-throw validation
solEscalationTriggers: Any ambiguity or implementation that permits caller-supplied authority, treats descriptor validation as authentication/authorization/dispatch, exposes Staff/AI publicly, shares guest/internal boundaries, makes booking availability depend on Staff/AI, or imports provider/infrastructure details into core.

Any provider/account/domain selection, credential or live authentication behavior, network/service/storage/queue/workflow/rate-limit/quota/deployment implementation, production write, guest-data retention, SQL, migration, RLS, payment, inventory, or pricing behavior.
rollbackExpectations: Revert only the P2-005 schema, canonical policy, deep module, validator, product documentation, task state/evidence, and P2-005 risk entry; preserve ADR-0002, GOV-043/GOV-047/GOV-048 history, terminal P1/P2 records and evidence, canonical sources, immutable snapshots, and all external systems.
